body: **Node 24 - unstable-super (Left) - Node 26 - feat2-super (Right)**

## Metrics: Node 26 (feat2) vs Node 24 (unstable, stable)

feat2 has run 763e246 on Node 26.13.0 since 2026-11-03 11:08 UTC. I compared it against unstable and stable on Node 24.22.x for the same node types: super, semi, solo, sas, mainnet-super.

**Method**
- Clean A/B: 2026-11-03 18:47 to 2026-11-04 07:47 UTC. unstable was running 14a10be, the base of this branch, so the Node version was the only difference.
- Second window: 2026-11-04 18:56 to 2026-11-05 07:56 UTC. unstable was 7 commits ahead.
- Host baseline: 2026-10-30/31, both groups on Node 24. This shows which feat2 vs unstable gaps come from the hosts and not from Node.

**Result: no functional regression. The only effect attributable to Node 26 is in GC.**

V8 new space halved. `nodejs_heap_space_size_total_bytes{space="new"}` dropped from 128 MiB to 64 MiB on every feat2 node, exactly at the deploy. New space is two semi-spaces, so that means 64 MiB per semi-space on Node 24 and 32 MiB on Node 26. The cause is V8 commit [8833da4](https://github.com/v8/v8/commit/8833da4379eaf3aca260c219c183b44fe87bdc19) ("[heap] Remove kPointerMultiplier"). The default max semi-space was `32 * kPointerMultiplier` MB, and `kPointerMultiplier = kTaggedSize / 4` is 2 on 64-bit builds without pointer compression. Node builds have pointer compression disabled (`process.config.variables.v8_enable_pointer_compression = 0` on both 24.22.2 and 26.13.0), so the default dropped from 64 MB to 32 MB per semi-space. The commit is in V8 14.6.202.34 (Node 26.13.0) and not in 13.6.233.17 (Node 24.22.2).

Effect vs stable over the last ~26h:

| | Node 24 (stable) | Node 26 (feat2) |
|---|---|---|
| minor GCs/s (super / mainnet-super) | 0.16 / 0.13 | 0.31 / 0.26 |
| avg minor GC pause | 11-13 ms | ~6 ms |
| avg major GC pause | 36-42 ms | 26-33 ms |
| GC pauses > 10 ms per hour (solo / super) | 300 / 352 | 135 / 211 |
| GC pauses > 100 ms per hour | 0.1-0.2 (super, mainnet-super) | ~0 |
| total GC time, % of wall time | 0.16-0.25% | 0.18-0.25% |

Total GC time is 8-11% higher on semi and mainnet-super, 3-10% on solo, and flat on super. In absolute terms that is about 0.015 percentage points of wall time. Pauses are shorter and there are fewer long pauses, so latency is not worse.

**No change beyond host noise:** gossip block to head, block STF and process time, epoch transition, head vote accuracy, inclusion distance, event loop lag, CPU, RSS, V8 heap, external memory, peers, gossip validation queue.

**Apparent improvements that are host effects:** on super, gossip validation job time is 56% lower, RSS is 30% lower, and STF is 5-16% faster. On semi, RSS is 30% lower. All of these already show up in the Node 24 vs Node 24 baseline. The unstable-super host also runs ~1.5 more cores of total load than feat2-super.

**sas:** windowed deltas look worse for event loop p99, gossip queue wait, req/resp errors and scrape duration. In the 6h time series, feat2-sas was already noisier than unstable-sas before the deploy, and only the GC rate steps at the switch. There is one sas node per group and no stable sas, so this stays inconclusive.

**Optional:** to restore the Node 24 young generation size, add `--max-semi-space-size=64` to `NODE_OPTIONS` and confirm new space reads 134217728 bytes. I have not validated this on a node; a local microbenchmark did not grow new space to its cap on either Node version. I don't think it should block this PR.

**Not covered:** arm64 and mainnet-fcr, which have no feat2 counterpart. Soak so far is ~47h.

body:
🤖 Thanks for tracking the semi-space change down. Added `--max-semi-space-size=64` next to `--max-old-space-size` in 86ec5cb64a (Dockerfile, Dockerfile.dev, `./lodestar`, docker-compose, standalone binaries).

Peak new space measured locally:

| | default | `--max-semi-space-size=64` |
|---|---|---|
| Node 24.22.1 | 128 MiB | 128 MiB |
| Node 26.13.0 | 64 MiB | 128 MiB |

So it restores Node 24 behaviour and is a no-op on 24. feat2 needs a redeploy with this build to confirm GC metrics line up with unstable. That should also tell us whether the `processEffectiveBalanceUpdates` bench regression comes from the semi-space change.
